claim: hasPermission(ClientModel, scope) only falls back to the 'Clients' (all-clients) resource when no per-client resource exists, so once any permission targets client X, all-clients permissions stop applying to X and admins granted e.g. manage on all clients lose access to X.

If the admin-permissions resource server has no 'Clients' type resource (realms initialized/exported before this PR), getResourceTypeResource returns null and findByResource(server, null) throws NullPointerException, turning client authorization checks into HTTP 500s.
body:
## [ISSUE] NPE when the `Clients` type resource does not exist (realms set up before this change)

**Severity:** MEDIUM — any client-level permission check by a non-role admin can return HTTP 500 on realms whose admin-permissions client was created before `CLIENTS` was added to the schema.

### The Problem

```java
resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);

if (authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) {
```

`getResourceTypeResource` returns `resourceStore.findByName(resourceServer, "Clients")` (`AdminPermissionsSchema.java:133`). That can return `null`. The code then passes the null to `findByResource`, and both store implementations dereference it: `StoreFactoryCacheSession.findByResource` calls `resource.getId()` (line 937) and `JPAPolicyStore.findByResource` calls `resource.getId()` (line 215).

### Theory / Proof

`AdminPermissionsSchema.init` creates the type resources only once, when the admin-permissions client is created, and returns early if `realm.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null` (lines 222-229). Realms that enabled admin permissions before this PR only have the `Users` resource. Realms imported from an older export through `RealmManager` (lines 566-571, `rep.getAdminPermissionsClient() != null`) also skip `init`. Nothing adds the new `Clients` resource later.

### What happens today vs. what will break

On a new realm, `init` creates `Clients` and the code works. On an existing or imported realm, an admin with only `query-users` who calls `GET /admin/realms/{realm}/clients` goes through `canView(c)` -> `canConfigure(c)` -> `canManage(c)` -> `hasPermission(c, MANAGE)` and gets an NPE, which becomes a 500. Creating an all-clients permission there also silently creates it without a resource (`AuthorizationProvider.java:323-327`, `if (resource != null)`).

### Research

The sibling `hasPermission(String scope)` in the same class guards against this with `if (resource == null) return false;` (lines 244-247). `UserPermissionsV2` shares the unguarded pattern, but `Users` has been in the schema since `init` was introduced, so its type resource is always there.

### Recommendation

Add a null guard, and preferably create missing type resources for realms where the admin-permissions client already exists:

```java
resource = AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(session, server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE);
if (resource == null || authz.getStoreFactory().getPolicyStore().findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) {
    return false;
}
```

claim: canView() only checks the all-clients VIEW scope, not MANAGE, so an admin granted MANAGE on all clients can create/delete clients and manage client scopes but gets 403 listing client scopes (requireListClientScopes/requireViewClientScopes) and cannot use the bulk list path.

getClientsWithPermission searches resources by type 'Clients', but per-client FGAP resources are created without a type, so it never returns real client IDs; it can only return the literal 'Clients' type-resource name, which the caller AvailableRoleMappingResource would pass to realm.getClientById() and NPE.

Gating the ProviderEventListener on the V1 feature means that under V2 nothing removes the per-client FGAP resource (named by client UUID) or its permissions when a client is deleted, leaving orphaned resources/permissions in the admin-permissions resource server.
